newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends little changed vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends little changed vs dollar.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended Thursday at 35.815/825 per dollar, little changed from Wednesday's close but some dealers said it could open lower on Friday after the finance minister.made some comments on the rupee.
"I would not like the rupee to strengthen because exporters will then complain," Finance Minister P.Chidambaram told Reuters.
The immediate impact could be a slight weakening of the rupee as corporates started covering exposures, said one dealer.
"But this may be a premature reaction," he cautioned. "Dollar inflows remain strong and we have to see what the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) does."
The rupee traded between a high of 35.815 and a low of 35.825 per dollar on Thursday, dealers said.
"Demand was poor and although the RBI bought dollars, supply was enough to meet their (RBI's) buying," said a dealer.
Dealers said the RBI bought in limited amounts and although precise figures were not available, they estimated the total central bank spot purchases on Thursday at $30-40 million.
They said the RBI bought both spot and forward dollars.
"In spot, they (RBI) bought between 35.82 and 35.825," said a dealer. "In forward, they bought outright end-May, end-June and end-July dollars."
Dealers said premiums on forward dollars rose after the RBI bought and later eased on selling of the US currency.
"The RBI buying pushed premiums up," said a dealer. "But some profit-taking at higher levels brought them down again almost to yesterday's closing levels."
November-deliver dollar ended Thursday at a premium of 86/88 paise against Wednesday's close of 85/87, dealers said.
